posts.text: @manngill thanks, this is a useful way to look at it, and it matches what management said on the Q4 FY26 call: Maarvel could not launch products, the new core went live in May 2025, and the retail and liability push is “starting now”, with the pick-up expected around Q4 FY27 / Q1 FY28. Two things from the decks, though. 1. It was not a straight decline from 2019. The 28.6% for Dec 2019 is right (Q3 FY20 deck). But CASA then went up to 35.1% by Jun 2022, on the same Maarvel system, and has come down to 19.0% since. So the rise and the fall look more like the rate cycle plus a balance sheet grow…

posts.community: CSB BANK - will it become next HDFC Bank?
posts.text: The CASA strategy reveals management’s philosophical orientation. CSB’s CASA ratio has actually declined from 28.6% in December 2019 to approximately 20% in Q4 FY26, a trajectory that would alarm most banking analysts. Management’s response has been characteristically direct. Mondal has stated: “Retail assets cannot be built without a CASA franchise because you need customers.” The bank is scaling its branch network and investing in technology specifically to build CASA organically through family banking, salary accounts, and digital channels, not by offering unsustainably high savings rates.…

posts.text: Following up on @Nishit_Shah2 ’s point about bulk deposits. Went through the Q2 FY27 investor presentation and press release (both filed 23 Oct) and the deposit side has moved the same way again. Headline numbers look good: deposits +18% YoY to ₹46,889 Cr, advances +22%, PAT +14% to ₹183 Cr. But look at what the deposit growth is made of. CASA was ₹8,394 Cr in Q2 FY26 and is ₹8,889 Cr now, only +6%. Term deposits went from ₹31,257 Cr to ₹38,000 Cr, +22%.
